narrative: The model estimated a 66% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that predicted risk was high, your law school application was denied; this does not mean failure is certain, but the school judged the risk too great to admit you. The strongest factor was your Year 1 class standing: you were in the third decile, compared with an accepted-student average around the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction toward failure. The second strongest factor was your LSAT score of 43, which is above the accepted-student average of about 37 and therefore pushed toward passing; it helped, but not enough to offset the academic-standing concerns. The third factor was your Year 3 standing, also third decile versus an accepted average near the sixth decile, which again pushed toward failure. To improve your position, ask admissions for feedback, strengthen your academic record or explain any relevant circumstances, and consider retaking the LSAT only if practice scores show a clear gain. Applying to programs whose admitted profiles better match your record would also improve your chances.
